title: A Two-Track Property Stabilization
text:
A Two-Track Property Stabilization

Xiaoxi Zhang

Gavekal Dragonomics | 7 Oct 2026

An end to China’s long-running decline in housing prices now appears in sight, at least for one corner of the market. Prices of both new and existing housing in the four Tier 1 cities of Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou and Shenzhen—China’s richest and most desirable property markets—have stabilized and even rebounded some in recent months. The Tier 1 cities have long been seen as a leading indicator for the national market, so this is certainly a positive signal. Nevertheless, the supply-demand dynamics in the Tier 1 cities are different and much more favorable than elsewhere. Many other cities overbuilt more and have less sticky demand, so their housing prices will continue to face pressure from oversupply for years. The turning point for Tier 1 cities is probably not going to be followed by a similar turning point for other cities, but rather by an ever-wider divergence in prices and performance.
